Creating a procedure/method is a form of abstraction. Allowing it to accept parameters is a form of generalization (by allowing it to be used for a number of similar inputs). stories.summary: The article distinguishes between two types of abstraction in system design: modularity abstraction (which hides implementation details through interfaces and encapsulation) and modeling abstraction (which reduces systems to their minimal behavioral essence relevant to a specific property). Examples of modeling abstraction include logical clocks, consensus protocols, and log-based databases.
